product_brief: A low SWaP, re-programmable IFF crypto appliqué for UAVs, supporting Mode 5 IFF Option B and NSA CM2 quantum-resistant requirements.
pqc_support: Planned — KIV-80 enables quantum resistant Crypto Modernization 2.0 (CM2) security; submitted to NSA for certification 1Q 2026.
pqc_capability_description: The product is designed to meet Crypto Modernization 2.0 (CM2) and is described as "NSA CM2 Quantum Resistant Compliant." It supports re-programmable algorithms and is upgradeable with the Advanced INFOSEC Machine (AIM) III crypto processor. Specific PQC algorithm names (e.g., ML-KEM, ML-DSA) are not listed in the text.
key_management_model: Hardware key storage with three months of black keys with key recovery; keys filled via DS-101 using an SKL or similar key fill device.
architecture_type: Hardware appliqué (2.5" W x 2.55" D x 0.8" H), ruggedized, sealed chassis, field replaceable battery, legacy adapter available.
primary_platforms: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), SWaP-constrained platforms, legacy IFF equipment (AIMS 04-900 Option B).
regulatory_status: Under NSA certification evaluation as KIV-80; submitted to NSA for certification 1Q 2026.
pqc_roadmap_details: Designed to meet Crypto Modernization 2.0 (CM2) per NSA requirements for software protection and algorithms; NSA certification submission targeted for 1Q 2026.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for SWaP-constrained platforms and UAVs; dimensions 2.5" W x 2.55" D x 0.8" H; weight 4.25 ounces; operational power 1100 mW nominal; battery life 8 years nominal.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Adapter for legacy crypto replacement; physically compatible with AIMS 04-900 Option B Mechanical Form Factor; legacy DS-101 Key Fill "audio" receptacle connector (U-229) available.

product_brief: A quantum-ready hardware wallet designed to safeguard cryptocurrency keys against future quantum threats.
pqc_support: Yes — Boardloader uses SLH-DSA-128; device attestation uses ML-DSA-44.
pqc_capability_description: The device is quantum-ready from startup. The boardloader uses a hybrid scheme with SLH-DSA-128 (SPHINCS+) and EdDSA (Ed25519) for firmware verification. Device authenticity is proven via a post-quantum certificate using ML-DSA-44. Certificates are distributed across three chips: OPTIGA Trust M (ECDSA), TROPIC01 (EdDSA), and STM32U5 (ML-DSA-44).
key_management_model: Hardware key storage with distributed device certificates across three independent chips (OPTIGA Trust M, TROPIC01, STM32U5) for redundancy.
architecture_type: Hardware security module (USB token) with multi-chip architecture (OPTIGA Trust M, TROPIC01, STM32U5).
pqc_roadmap_details: NIST aims to define a framework for worldwide transition by 2035. Trezor Safe 7 is designed to run post-quantum updates, but these updates do not exist yet. The boardloader is ready to verify post-quantum firmware updates.

product_brief: Automotive microcontroller with ISO/SAE 21434 compliance and PQC capabilities for secure boot and OTA updates.
pqc_support: Yes — AURIX TC49 is already PQC-capable; capability is being extended across the AURIX TC4x and TRAVEO T2G families.
pqc_capability_description: The AURIX TC49 integrates dedicated CPUs, non-volatile memory (NVM), and hardware accelerators to support efficient PQC use cases. Specific applications include secured boot processes and secured Over-the-Air (OTA) software updates within the Software-Defined Vehicle ecosystem.
key_management_model: Hardware-based key storage using non-volatile memory (NVM) and dedicated CPUs.
architecture_type: Automotive Microcontroller (MCU) with dedicated CPUs, NVM, and hardware accelerators.
regulatory_status: ISO/SAE 21434 compliant; CATARC-Cybersecurity-Zertifizierung (for AURIX TC397, TC49 implied in family context); UNECE R155 and R156 compliance support.
pqc_roadmap_details: PQC capability is being extended across the entire AURIX TC4x and TRAVEO T2G families. The AURIX TC49 (introduced Feb 2026) is already PQC-capable, with further AURIX TC4x derivatives to follow.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for automotive microcontrollers; integrates dedicated CPUs and NVM for efficient PQC execution in constrained embedded environments.
